hypothesis: Advanced temporal and hybrid models that explicitly capture quantum–classical temporal dynamics (sequence models, autoencoders/VAEs, graph-based context, and hybrid anomaly+supervised stacks) will achieve significantly better attack/anomaly detection performance on quantum-network-like telemetry than the baseline models from Chapter 8, for comparable or acceptable increases in computational and latency overhead suitable for near-real-time deployment.

baseline.description: Baseline models trained in Chapter 8 on the same quantum-network-like datasets, using non-temporal or weakly-temporal classical ML approaches.

models.name: IForest-Static
models.input_representation: Per-window aggregated feature vectors over quantum and classical metrics (e.g., means, variances, simple deltas for QBER, key rate, loss), flattened; no explicit sequence structure.
models.training_target: Normal-only training (unlabeled or majority-normal data) with anomaly scores at inference.

models.name: RF-Static
models.input_representation: Same per-window aggregated features as IForest-Static.
models.training_target: Multi-class labels indicating {benign, eavesdropping, jamming, misconfiguration, other attack} at window level.

treatment.description: Advanced temporal and hybrid models designed to capture fine-grained temporal behavior, rare event structure, and graph/topological context in quantum networks, and to fuse unsupervised anomaly scores with supervised classifiers.

models.name: TCN-Seq
models.algorithm: Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) implemented in PyTorch
models.input_representation: Fixed-length sequences of per-timestep feature vectors (e.g., 60 time steps × F features, where each step corresponds to a small time-slice from the simulator). Features include quantum metrics (QBER, sifted key rate, channel loss, timing variance) and synchronized classical metrics (link utilization, control-plane error counts, alarms).
models.training_target: Sequence-level prediction indicating whether the window contains an attack or anomaly; optionally finer-grained timestep-level labels for auxiliary loss.

models.name: LSTM-Seq
models.input_representation: Same as TCN-Seq: sequences of per-timestep quantum+classical features.
models.training_target: Sequence-level binary/multi-class classification for attack vs. benign, optionally attack type.

models.name: AE-Window
models.algorithm: Fully connected autoencoder implemented in PyTorch
models.input_representation: Per-window aggregated feature vectors (same dimensionality as baselines) using only windows labeled as benign for training.
models.training_target: Reconstruction of input; anomaly score derived from reconstruction error.

models.name: VAE-Window
models.type: Variational autoencoder for rare event detection
models.algorithm: VAE implemented in PyTorch with Gaussian latent variables
models.input_representation: Same per-window aggregated features as AE-Window.
models.training_target: Variational reconstruction objective (reconstruction loss + KL divergence); anomaly score using negative ELBO or reconstruction error.

models.name: Hybrid-IForest-RF
models.algorithm: Pipeline combining IForest anomaly scores and RF classifier
models.input_representation: Per-window aggregated features plus appended unsupervised anomaly scores (from IForest or AE/VAE) as additional features to a supervised classifier.
models.training_target: Supervised multi-class classification over attacks and benign, with class imbalance handling.

key_hyperparameters.supervised_component: GradientBoostingClassifier or RandomForest with tuned depth
key_hyperparameters.calibration: Platt scaling or isotonic regression on validation set

models.name: Graph-Context-GCN
models.algorithm: Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) or GraphSAGE implemented using PyTorch Geometric
models.input_representation: Time-sliced quantum network graphs where nodes represent network elements (QKD links, trusted nodes, repeaters, classical routers) with node feature vectors (local quantum/classical metrics aggregated over a short interval), and edges represent physical or logical connectivity with edge features (link-specific metrics).
models.training_target: Node-level or edge-level binary labels indicating presence of anomalous/attacked behavior in that time slice; optionally aggregated to sequence-level decision for the entire path or link.

models.name: Latency-Optimized-TCN-Lite
models.algorithm: Shallower TCN or 1D CNN sequence classifier implemented in PyTorch
models.input_representation: Shorter sequences (e.g., 20 time steps) and reduced feature set focusing on most informative quantum metrics.
models.training_target: Binary detection (attack vs. benign) optimized for inference latency and CPU-only deployment.

workloads.name: WL-1-SingleLink-Temporal-Attacks
workloads.description: Simulated single QKD link with temporally localized attacks and failures to emphasize time dynamics.
workloads.data_source: Chapter 6 simulator (Python) configured for a single logical QKD link with classical control channel.

channels: Single BB84-like QKD link with decoy states

attack_scenarios.pattern: short bursts (5–10 min) at random times

benign_failures.effect: loss increase, moderate key rate drop, minimal QBER impact
small correlated variations in QBER, loss, and timing

dataset_preparation.labels: Window or sequence labeled attack type if any timestep overlaps attack interval; otherwise benign.

splits.train: First 60% of timeline with attacks restricted to defined windows
splits.val: Next 20% of timeline with a mix of known attacks and benign drifts
splits.test: Last 20% of timeline containing unseen combinations and timings of attacks/failures

workloads.name: WL-2-MultiLink-Topology-Context
workloads.description: Simulated small quantum network (3–8 QKD links, 2–4 trusted nodes, classical backbone) to test topology-aware detection.
workloads.data_source: Chapter 6 simulator extended to multi-link scenario with network topology and routing.

configuration.topology: Small meshed topology with at least one redundant path between endpoints and a mix of direct QKD links and repeater-based paths.

attack_scenarios.pattern: simultaneous partial jamming on multiple adjacent links to mimic wide-area interference
attack_scenarios.targets: two neighboring QKD links sharing a trusted node
attack_scenarios.effect: correlated changes across nodes and edges

attack_scenarios.pattern: persistent misconfiguration at a trusted node causing abnormal routing or key usage
attack_scenarios.effect: anomalous patterns localized to node and adjacent edges

benign_variation.effect: changes in classical utilization without quantum anomalies
temporary shutdown of one link with clean alarms

graph_slices.labels: Node or edge labeled anomalous if part of an attack scenario within the slice; benign otherwise.

splits.train: Random 60% of graph slices, ensuring at least 30% of benign-only slices
splits.val: 20% of slices, disjoint time ranges from train
splits.test: 20% of slices including unseen combinations of attacks and benign patterns

workloads.name: WL-3-Rare-Attack-Events
workloads.description: Dataset with extreme class imbalance and rare, subtle attack patterns to test autoencoders/VAEs and hybrid stacks.
workloads.data_source: Chapter 6 simulator with attack frequency tuned to reflect rare events.

configuration.attack_frequency: attack windows < 1% of total time overall

attack_scenarios.pattern: minimal QBER increase but subtle changes in joint distribution of key rate and timing jitter
small persistent drifts causing downstream key management anomalies

configuration.benign_background: Diverse benign conditions including variable classical load, environmental noise, and normal maintenance.

features: aggregated_statistics_over_window (mean, std, min, max) for all primary quantum and classical metrics
trend_features (slope estimates) for qber and key_rate

dataset_preparation.labels: Binary rare-event indicator per window; separate multi-class label where possible for analyses.

splits.train: Normal-only windows (no attack overlap) for AE/VAE; for hybrid classifiers, include slightly more positives but still imbalanced, e.g., 1–2% positive class.
splits.val: Mixture with approx. 5% positive windows to support threshold tuning.
splits.test: Natural class distribution from simulator (~1% attack windows).

preprocessing.normalization: StandardScaler or RobustScaler fitted on training data only; scaler objects persisted and reused for val/test.
preprocessing.feature_selection: Identical input feature sets for baselines and treatments wherever model architecture allows; when reduced (e.g., latency-optimized model), record subset explicitly.

training_protocol.cross_validation: Single fixed train/val split used consistently for hyperparameter selection; hyperparameter search limited to predefined grids and documented.
training_protocol.early_stopping: Validation loss or F1-based early stopping with patience defined per model; selection criterion recorded.
training_protocol.class_imbalance: Consistent handling across models: class_weight='balanced' for classical models, weighted loss for deep models; sampling strategies (e.g., focal loss or oversampling) documented when used.

evaluation_protocol.test_set_isolation: Test sets untouched until final evaluation; no hyperparameter tuning or threshold selection using test metrics.
evaluation_protocol.threshold_selection: For anomaly scores and probabilistic outputs, thresholds tuned on validation data only, using standardized strategies (e.g., maximize F1, or fixed recall target).
evaluation_protocol.repetitions: Each deep model training repeated N=3 runs with different seeds {0,1,2}; report mean and std for core metrics.

hardware.baseline_env: Single workstation or cloud instance with 8 vCPUs, 32 GB RAM, and a single GPU (e.g., NVIDIA T4 or equivalent) for deep models; CPU-only baseline runs for latency comparison.
hardware.gpu_usage: GPU used only for deep sequence/graph models during training; inference benchmarks measured separately on CPU and GPU when relevant.

metrics.name: attack_detection_auroc
metrics.description: Area under the ROC curve for attack/anomaly detection at the window/sequence level on the test set.

metrics.name: attack_detection_aupr
metrics.description: Area under the precision–recall curve for the positive (attack/anomaly) class; especially important under class imbalance (WL-3).

metrics.name: attack_recall_at_fixed_fpr
metrics.description: Recall of attack/anomaly windows at a fixed false positive rate (e.g., FPR = 1% on validation-tuned threshold).

metrics.name: macro_f1
metrics.description: Macro-averaged F1-score over benign and attack classes, or over all attack types for multi-class tasks.

metrics.name: rare_event_detection_rate
metrics.description: For WL-3, proportion of rare attack windows correctly flagged at or below a given FPR threshold.

metrics.name: inference_latency_p50
metrics.description: Median end-to-end inference time (including preprocessing) measured on CPU and, where applicable, GPU.

metrics.name: inference_latency_p95
metrics.description: 95th percentile end-to-end inference time; primary latency SLO indicator.

metrics.name: throughput_windows_per_second
metrics.description: Sustainable throughput for batched inference, measured under steady load on CPU and/or GPU.

metrics.name: model_size
metrics.description: On-disk size of the persisted model parameters and architecture configuration.

metrics.name: training_time
metrics.description: Wall-clock training time until early stopping for each model on specified hardware.

primary: On WL-1 (single-link temporal), at least one temporal model (TCN-Seq or LSTM-Seq) achieves >= 5 percentage-point absolute improvement in attack_recall_at_fixed_fpr (FPR = 1%) over RF-Static, with test attack_detection_aupr also improved by >= 0.05 absolute.
On WL-3 (rare event), AE-Window or VAE-Window achieves >= 0.10 absolute improvement in rare_event_detection_rate at FPR <= 1% compared to IForest-Static, when thresholds are tuned on validation data.
Hybrid-IForest-RF (or hybrid using AE/VAE scores) achieves higher macro_f1 (>= 0.03 absolute increase) than RF-Static alone on WL-3, while keeping inference_latency_p95 increase <= 50% on CPU.
secondary: Graph-Context-GCN on WL-2 shows improved localization of attacks (node/edge-level detection) compared to RF-Static applied independently at link level, as measured by at least 0.05 higher macro_f1 on anomalous vs. benign nodes or edges.
Latency-Optimized-TCN-Lite meets a target inference_latency_p95 <= 10 ms per sequence on CPU for WL-1 while maintaining attack_detection_aupr within 0.03 of full TCN-Seq.
For at least one temporal model, improvement in AUROC/AUPR over baselines remains consistent (difference in metric >= 0.03) across all three runs with different random seeds.

failure_modes.name: overfitting_temporal_models
failure_modes.description: Temporal models show excellent validation performance but degraded or baseline-equivalent performance on the held-out test set, suggesting overfitting to particular attack timing patterns.
failure_modes.detection: Validation metrics substantially higher than test, or large variance across random seeds; learning curves that diverge after few epochs.
mitigations: Simplify model architectures (fewer layers, smaller hidden sizes).
Augment training data with varied attack timing and noise configurations.

failure_modes.name: collapsed_vae_latent_space
failure_modes.description: VAE learns trivial encoding where latent variables carry little information, leading to poor separation between normal and anomalous reconstruction errors.
failure_modes.detection: KL term dominates or vanishes; reconstruction errors for benign and attack windows share similar distributions on validation data.
mitigations: Adjust beta parameter in beta-VAE objective.
Modify architecture (larger latent dimension, deeper encoder/decoder).
Warm-up schedule for KL term or alternative priors.

failure_modes.name: instability_with_extreme_class_imbalance
failure_modes.description: Models trained on WL-3 fail to converge to useful detectors due to highly imbalanced labels.
failure_modes.detection: Models predict majority class for nearly all windows; near-zero recall on attack windows despite good accuracy.
mitigations: Apply limited oversampling or synthetic minority oversampling for supervised components.
Train unsupervised components strictly on benign data and reframe task as anomaly detection.

failure_modes.name: graph_model_scalability_limits
failure_modes.description: Graph-based models become prohibitively slow or memory-intensive as the number of nodes/edges or timesteps increases.
failure_modes.detection: Out-of-memory errors, excessively long training or inference times, or failure to meet latency targets.
mitigations: Reduce graph size via subgraph extraction (e.g., ego-graphs around suspect nodes).
Use sampling-based GNNs (GraphSAGE) instead of full-batch GCN.
Aggregate temporal information before graph construction to reduce graph rate.

failure_modes.name: misleading_latency_measurements
failure_modes.description: Latency benchmarks are measured under unrealistic conditions (e.g., warm cache, no preprocessing) and do not reflect SOC deployment reality.
failure_modes.detection: Significant discrepancy between benchmarked latency and prototype pipeline measurements (Chapter 10).
mitigations: Include feature preprocessing and model inference in latency benchmarks.
Measure latency over long runs with realistic batch sizes and mixed benign/attack traffic.
Separate cold-start latency from steady-state latency.

software.os: Linux (Ubuntu 22.04 LTS recommended) or equivalent container base image
core_packages: torchvision>=0.16,<0.18 (for compatibility, though not strictly required)
torch-geometric and related dependencies aligned with torch version

hardware.gpu: Optional but recommended for deep models (e.g., NVIDIA T4, V100, or equivalent with >= 8GB VRAM).
hardware.storage: At least 20 GB free disk space to store generated datasets, models, and logs.

run_instructions.overview: The experiment consists of three main phases: (1) data generation using the Chapter 6 simulator configured for the Chapter 9 workloads, (2) dataset preparation using the Chapter 7 pipelines adapted for sequences and graphs, and (3) training and evaluating baseline vs. advanced models, including latency and complexity benchmarks.

steps.title: Clone repository and set up environment
notes: requirements_ch09.txt should pin versions compatible with this experiment, including PyTorch and PyTorch Geometric.
If GPU is available, install the CUDA-enabled PyTorch build per official instructions and ensure torch.cuda.is_available() returns True.

steps.title: Generate simulated data for workloads WL-1, WL-2, and WL-3
notes: Each config file defines simulation duration, time resolution, attack schedules, and logging options.
Set RNG seeds in the config or via environment variable (e.g., SIM_SEED=42) to ensure reproducibility.
Monitor generated log sizes; adjust duration if storage constraints are tight, but keep relative attack frequency and patterns similar.

steps.title: Prepare ML-ready datasets (sequences, windows, graphs)
notes: These scripts should implement the windowing and labeling schemes described under workloads, including sequence length, stride, feature extraction, and label assignment.
Ensure that train/val/test splits are created exactly once and saved (e.g., as index files or split manifests) to avoid data leakage.
Output formats: PyTorch tensors (.pt) or NumPy arrays (.npz) for sequence/window data; for graphs, PyTorch Geometric data objects serialized per slice or batched.

steps.title: Run baseline models on Chapter 9 datasets
notes: Use the same feature sets as for Chapter 8 where possible; for temporal data, derive aggregated features per window consistent with baseline assumptions.
Store trained baseline models and metrics in results/ch09/baselines/ to enable direct comparison.

steps.title: Train and evaluate temporal models (TCN-Seq, LSTM-Seq, Latency-Optimized-TCN-Lite)
notes: Each run should save: model checkpoints, training logs, validation metrics per epoch, final test metrics, and latency benchmarks.
Latency benchmarks: use a separate script or mode (e.g., --benchmark-latency) to evaluate inference_latency_p50/p95 and throughput on CPU and, optionally, GPU.

steps.title: Train and evaluate autoencoder and VAE models on rare-event dataset
notes: Ensure that AE/VAE training uses only benign windows from the training split.
After training, run anomaly scoring on val/test splits and compute AUROC, AUPR, rare_event_detection_rate, and threshold-dependent metrics.
Store reconstruction error distributions and score histograms for later analysis.

steps.title: Train and evaluate hybrid models combining anomaly scores with supervised classifiers
notes: The hybrid script should first compute and persist anomaly scores for all train/val/test windows, then augment feature vectors with these scores before training the supervised classifier.
Calibration of predicted probabilities (e.g., Platt scaling) should be performed on the validation split and applied at test time.

steps.title: Train and evaluate graph-based contextual model
notes: Use PyTorch Geometric loaders for graph slices.
Evaluate both node-level and edge-level detection metrics; store confusion matrices and per-node/edge scores.
For complexity analysis, vary number of layers or hidden dimensions via config to observe performance vs. complexity trade-offs.

steps.title: Aggregate metrics and compare treatments with baselines
notes: The aggregation script should produce tables and plots comparing AUROC, AUPR, recall at fixed FPR, macro F1, latency, throughput, model size, and training time across baselines and advanced models.
Ensure that statistical summaries (mean, std across seeds) are computed and stored for temporal models.

steps.title: Optional: Run Chapter 9 Jupyter notebook for interactive exploration
notes: The notebook should load precomputed metrics and provide visualizations (ROC/PR curves, latency vs. performance plots) and code snippets explaining key design trade-offs.
Interactive widgets can allow adjusting thresholds and observing impact on operational metrics like alert rate.

evidence_schema.description: Schema for capturing and storing experimental results to enable rigorous comparison and reproducibility, without encoding any specific outcomes.

fields.dataset_version: string or hash identifying the exact dataset/preprocessing version
fields.notes: optional string with free-form comments about run conditions or anomalies

config_file.fields: Complete snapshot of all hyperparameters, data paths, and environment settings used for the run.

fields.baseline_results: array of aggregated metric objects per baseline model and workload (mean, std, sample_count)
fields.treatment_results: array of aggregated metric objects per treatment model and workload
fields.comparisons: array of objects describing differences between baselines and treatments for each metric, including confidence intervals or effect sizes where computed

baseline_treatment_linking.approach: For each workload and metric, link baselines and treatments via common workload key and metric names; comparisons computed as treatment_metric - baseline_metric for chosen baselines.
